mainTopic: רבי יצחק on תרומה-level purity and fourth-level impurity in קודש; רב אסי on whether, for רבי שמעון, שחיטה or blood makes meat susceptible to impurity
overview: The גמרא finishes a discussion about whether the rule 'purity kept at the תרומה level counts as impurity for קודש' applies to food as well as clothing. רבי יצחק says it does. רבי ירמיה מדיפתי challenges him from a משנה about holy wine poured into a barrel of תרומה wine. רבי יצחק answers that a mixed barrel is a special case of trust (מגו). Next, רב הונא בר נתן brings a source in which non-sacred food kept at קודש-level purity can disqualify holy food. The גמרא answers that this is a dispute between תנאים. Then the גמרא turns to רבי שמעון in the משנה, and רב אסי explains that for רבי שמעון the שחיטה, not the blood, makes the meat susceptible to impurity. Proofs for and against רב אסי are each pushed off, mainly by contrasting the blood of killed animals with the blood of a dead animal or a wound. The גמרא ends by bringing the פסוק behind blood of killed animals, and it explains that the 'like water' פסוק about blood of שחיטה teaches a different law.

steps.title: Clothing versus food: how far the rule reaches
steps.stepSummary: The rule that תרומה-level purity counts as impure for קודש applies to clothing, because of the worry about a נדה wife. Some limit it to clothing. רבי יצחק applies it to food as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: With clothing we worry that his wife sat on them while she was a נדה. But with produce we don't say this rule. רבי יצחק, however, says it about produce too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation already in progress. It shows that one view applies the rule only to clothing, while רבי יצחק applies it to food too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothing has a special risk: his wife may have sat on it while she was a נדה, and that would make it impure. Food has no such risk, so one view says the rule stops at clothing. רבי יצחק extends it to food anyway, and the next steps challenge him on this.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her menstrual state, who makes things she sits on impure
Produce, meaning food items
We do not say this (the rule does not apply)

phrases.english: lest his wife sit upon them while she is a niddah,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the clothing of someone who keeps תרומה-level purity, from the discussion just before this.

phrases.english: but regarding produce we do not say this.
And Rabbi Yitzchak says it regarding produce as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation that was in progress before this section began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'תרומה-level purity is impurity for קודש' rule applies to clothing because of the נדה worry. רבי יצחק applies it to food too.

steps.title: Challenge from the barrel of תרומה wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה מדיפתי brings a משנה. An עם הארץ is believed when he says he put holy wine into his תרומה barrel. That suggests the תרומה does not make the קודש impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really say this about produce? We learned in a משנה: if he says 'I put a רביעית of holy wine into it,' he is believed, and the תרומה does not make the קודש impure. If the purity of תרומה counted as impurity for קודש, the תרומה should make the קודש impure!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה מדיפתי attacks רבי יצחק's view that the rule also applies to food. He uses a משנה about wine in a barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the holy wine sits inside תרומה wine and is still treated as pure. If תרומה-level food counted as impure for קודש, the holy wine in that barrel would become impure. So the משנה seems to show that the rule does not apply to food.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג, a small liquid measure
Sacred food or drink, such as sacrificial items
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Believed (trusted)
Its purity counts as impurity when it comes to קודש

steps.confusionAlert: The holy wine is not a separate item next to the barrel. It is poured into the very same barrel as the תרומה. That is exactly why the משנה seems to be a strong challenge.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti raises an objection:
And do we really say this regarding produce?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
phrases.notes: חגיגה 24b. An עם הארץ is talking about his barrel of תרומה wine.

phrases.english: If he said: "I separated into it
a quarter-log of holy wine" – he is believed,
and the terumah does not make the holy wine impure.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, and it means the same thing.

phrases.english: And if you say:
its purity is impurity with regard to holy food –
then let the terumah make the holy wine impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יצחק's view from step 1 that the rule also applies to food.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that תרומה-level food counts as impure for קודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה treats holy wine mixed into תרומה wine as pure. That should be impossible if תרומה-level food were impure for קודש.

steps.title: A mixed barrel is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that items joined together are different. Since the עם הארץ is believed about the holy wine, he must also be believed about the תרומה it is mixed with.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you bringing a case of impurity with joined items? Joined items are different. Since he is believed about the קודש, he is believed about the תרומה too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק defends himself. He says the barrel case is an exception and does not prove anything about food in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holy wine and the תרומה wine are in one barrel and cannot be separated. Once we trust the person about the קודש, we have to trust him about the תרומה mixed with it. This is a מגו. So the משנה only teaches about trust in a mixed barrel, and רבי יצחק's general rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity in items joined together, here wines mixed in one barrel
Is different
Since: because we accept one claim, we accept the connected one too
Is trusted

steps.whatToRemember: The barrel משנה is explained as a special case of trust (a מגו) in mixed items. It does not prove that תרומה-level food is fine for קודש, so רבי יצחק's view survives.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יצחק answering רבי ירמיה מדיפתי.

phrases.english: You are speaking of impurity with joined items?
phrases.notes: "Joined" here means the two wines are mixed together in one barrel.

phrases.english: Impurity with joined items is different,
since he is believed about the holy wine –
he is believed about the terumah as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the proof to a special case (mixed items and trust)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel משנה seemed to show that תרומה never makes קודש impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about trusting someone with a mixed barrel. It says nothing about food in general.

steps.title: Challenge from the levels of impurity in non-sacred food
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר נתן quotes a ברייתא. Non-sacred food prepared at קודש-level purity, when it is at the third level of impurity, can still disqualify holy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר נתן objects: Non-sacred food at the second level makes non-sacred liquid impure and disqualifies תרומה food. Non-sacred food at the third level makes holy liquid impure and disqualifies holy food, when the non-sacred food was prepared at the purity level of קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to רבי יצחק begins. רב הונא בר נתן quotes a source that seems to clash with רבי יצחק's view that only real קודש can create a fourth level of impurity in קודש. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק had said that only real קודש can create a fourth level of impurity in קודש. This ברייתא says that a third-level item can disqualify holy food, which gives the holy food a fourth level. And here the item doing it is non-sacred food that was only prepared at קודש-level purity, which seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: The second level of impurity
The third level of impurity
Ordinary, non-sacred food
A liquid, which becomes impure more easily than solid food
Disqualifies: makes it unfit, but it does not pass impurity on
Non-sacred food prepared as carefully as if it were holy

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different verbs here. 'מטמא' means the liquid becomes impure and can pass impurity on. 'פוסל' means the food becomes unfit but does not pass impurity any further.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Natan raises an objection:
Second-level impurity in non-sacred food makes non-sacred liquid impure,
and disqualifies terumah foods,
and the third level makes holy liquid impure,
and disqualifies holy foods,
in non-sacred food that was prepared at the purity level of holy food.
phrases.notes: This last line applies to the third-level case just before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge to רבי יצחק, this time about a fourth level of impurity in קודש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's view that only real קודש can create a fourth level of impurity in קודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows that non-sacred food prepared at קודש-level purity, at the third level, can disqualify holy food and so create a fourth level.

steps.title: The issue is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that other תנאים disagree with the ברייתא of רב הונא בר נתן. A ברייתא brings two views: one says חולין kept at קודש-level purity are like ordinary חולין, and רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says they are like תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: Non-sacred food that was prepared at the purity level of holy food is treated like ordinary non-sacred food. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: it is treated like תרומה. An impure item can make two levels of it impure, and the next level only becomes disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 4. It says the question is a dispute between תנאים, and it quotes a ברייתא that disagrees with the source רב הונא בר נתן brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 the ברייתא said this kind of food can reach a third level of impurity and disqualify holy food. In this new ברייתא, the first view treats it like plain חולין, so it never reaches a third level. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק treats it like תרומה, so it reaches a third level but goes no further. Since תנאים argue about this, the source from Step 4 is only one side of the dispute and cannot decide the question against רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים, the sages of the משנה era
The strict purity level kept for holy food
To make two levels impure (first and second level)
To disqualify one more level (third level), which does not pass impurity on further

steps.confusionAlert: Both views in this ברייתא agree that this food does not reach the level of disqualifying holy food in the way the Step 4 source said. They only disagree about whether it is like plain חולין or like תרומה.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between tanna'im, as it is taught:
Non-sacred food that was prepared at the purity level of holy food
is like ordinary non-sacred food.
phrases.notes: Ordinary חולין can't go past a second level of impurity, so it never reaches a third level.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
It is like teruma,
so an impure source makes two levels impure, and the next one is only disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב הונא בר נתן's ברייתא in Step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: the challenging source is only one side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא from Step 4 seemed to be the accepted rule and seemed to work against רבי יצחק
steps.terutzMaskana: Other תנאים disagree, so that ברייתא does not settle the question
steps.whatToRemember: When the גמרא says תנאי היא, it means the challenging source is just one opinion among the תנאים, so it cannot force a decision.

steps.title: רב אסי explains רבי שמעון: the שחיטה makes it susceptible, not the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about an animal slaughtered with no blood coming out. רבי שמעון said it became susceptible to impurity through the שחיטה. רב אסי explains that for רבי שמעון it is the שחיטה, and not the blood, that does this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: They were made susceptible to impurity through the slaughter. רב אסי said: רבי שמעון used to say that its slaughter makes it susceptible, and not the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting רבי שמעון from the משנה. Then רב אסי explains exactly what רבי שמעון meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food normally can only become impure after it gets wet from a liquid, and blood counts as such a liquid. In the משנה no blood came out, and רבי שמעון said the שחיטה itself makes the meat susceptible. רב אסי adds more: for רבי שמעון, only the שחיטה does it, and the blood does not.

keyTerms.meaning: They were made susceptible (able) to become ritually impure
Kosher ritual slaughter
Makes something susceptible to impurity

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: They were made susceptible through the slaughter.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה on 33a, about an animal that was slaughtered but no blood came out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: Rav Asi said: Rabbi Shimon used to say,
its slaughter makes it susceptible, and not the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, separate from the purity-levels discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the שחיטה makes the meat susceptible to impurity, and the blood does not

steps.title: Trying to prove רב אסי from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון's words in the משנה support רב אסי. It asks whether 'through the slaughter' means only the slaughter and not the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say the משנה supports him: רבי שמעון says they were made susceptible through the slaughter. Doesn't that mean through the slaughter and not through the blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove רב אסי's explanation from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is based on the fact that רבי שמעון named only the שחיטה. The גמרא suggests that naming only the שחיטה means the blood plays no role, which is exactly what רב אסי said.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this source supports him
Doesn't it mean...? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Let us say it supports him:
Rabbi Shimon says: They were made susceptible through the slaughter.
Doesn't it mean through the slaughter and not through the blood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support רב אסי's statement from Step 6
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's claim that for רבי שמעון the blood does not make it susceptible
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's words in the משנה: הוכשרו בשחיטה

steps.title: The proof is rejected: the שחיטה works too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי שמעון may mean that the שחיטה also makes it susceptible, in addition to the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means also through the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון named the שחיטה because in the משנה's case no blood came out. That does not prove the blood never works. He could mean the blood works and the שחיטה works too, so the משנה does not prove רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

phrases.english: No, also through the slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה; רב אסי's statement itself still stands
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'through the slaughter' means 'only through the slaughter,' but it can mean 'also through the slaughter'
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can be read two ways, so it does not prove רב אסי. His statement stands, but without support from the משנה.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to support רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון says it is not the blood but the שחיטה that makes the meat susceptible. This seems to support רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי שמעון said to the חכמים: Is it the blood that makes it susceptible to impurity? Isn't it the שחיטה that makes it susceptible!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to back up רב אסי. In it, רבי שמעון seems to say clearly that the blood does not make the meat susceptible, and the שחיטה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become impure after it gets wet with certain liquids, and blood is one of them. Here רבי שמעון seems to push away the blood entirely and give the job to the שחיטה, which is exactly רב אסי's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes something susceptible to impurity, so it can now become טמא
Kosher slaughter of an animal
But isn't it so that…, used to make a strong point

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Shimon said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the חכמים who argue with רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Is it the blood that makes it susceptible?
But isn't it the slaughter that makes it susceptible!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was rejected in Step 8, the גמרא tries a second proof for רב אסי from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's claim that for רבי שמעון the שחיטה, not the blood, makes the meat susceptible
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון says: 'Is it the blood that makes it susceptible? Isn't it the שחיטה!'

steps.title: The ברייתא may mean slaughter also works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי שמעון may mean that blood is not the only thing that works, and the שחיטה works too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying to them: Is it only the blood that makes it susceptible? The שחיטה also makes it susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by reading רבי שמעון's words differently. He is not saying blood does nothing. He is saying blood is not the only thing that works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on reading 'Is it the blood?' as 'not the blood at all.' The גמרא reads it as 'not only the blood,' so both blood and שחיטה could make it susceptible. This is the same kind of answer as Step 8, and it leaves רב אסי without proof.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means, a way of re-reading someone's words
Only, alone
Also, too

phrases.english: This is what he is saying to them:
Is it blood alone that makes it susceptible?
Slaughter also makes it susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove רב אסי wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof read 'Is it the blood?' as 'not blood at all,' when it can mean 'not blood alone.'
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs for רב אסי (Steps 7 and 9) are pushed off the same way: רבי שמעון may hold that the שחיטה works in addition to the blood.

steps.title: Blood of an animal that died seems to imply slaughter blood works
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי שמעון holds that blood of a dead animal does not make things susceptible. That seems to imply that blood of שחיטה does, which goes against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי שמעון says: Blood of a dead animal does not make things susceptible. Doesn't that mean that blood of שחיטה does make things susceptible?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns around and attacks רב אסי. It brings a ברייתא and draws an inference from it that would mean, for רבי שמעון, the blood of שחיטה does work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון had to say that blood of an animal that died on its own does not work, it sounds like blood from a proper שחיטה does work. That would go against רב אסי, who said that for רבי שמעון the blood does not do it.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of an animal that died on its own (not slaughtered or killed)
Isn't it that…? Used to bring out an inference

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Shimon says:
Blood of the dead animal does not make things susceptible.
phrases.notes: He means an animal that died on its own.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, הָא דַּם שְׁחִיטָה מַכְשִׁיר?
phrases.english: Isn't it that this implies blood of slaughter does make things susceptible?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: דַּם הַמֵּת אֵינוֹ מַכְשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The attempts to support רב אסי have failed. Now the גמרא tries to disprove him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that for רבי שמעון the blood does not make the meat susceptible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'blood of a dead animal does not work' implies the opposite case, blood of שחיטה, does work.

steps.title: The opposite case may be blood of killed animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. The 'opposite case' may be blood of animals that were killed, not blood of שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the implication is that blood of killed animals makes things susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the attack. The ברייתא is contrasting a dead animal with a killed animal, not with a slaughtered one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inference only tells us that some other case is different. Here the other case can be animals that were killed (חללים), so the ברייתא says nothing about blood of שחיטה, and רב אסי can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of animals that were killed, as opposed to ones that died on their own

phrases.english: No, rather blood of killed animals makes things susceptible,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the inference drawn in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference against רב אסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference picked the wrong opposite case. The contrast can be with killed animals, not slaughtered ones.

steps.title: Then why not teach the slaughter case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the answer. If blood of שחיטה does not work, רבי שמעון should have said so, and we would know all the more so about a dead animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But blood of שחיטה, what? It does not make things susceptible? Then let him teach us about blood of שחיטה, and all the more so we would know about blood of a dead animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 12. If שחיטה blood also doesn't work, why did רבי שמעון pick the dead animal as his example?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of שחיטה seems stronger than blood of an animal that just died. If even שחיטה blood does not work, we would know by a כל שכן that dead-animal blood does not work. So mentioning the dead animal seems like the weaker, less useful example.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him teach us
All the more so, how much more

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דַּם שְׁחִיטָה מַאי – לָא מַכְשִׁיר?
phrases.english: But blood of slaughter, what? It does not make things susceptible?
Then let him teach us about blood of slaughter,
and all the more so blood of the dead animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל דַּם שְׁחִיטָה מַאי – לָא מַכְשִׁיר? לַישְׁמְעִינַן דַּם שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא contrasts a dead animal with killed animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שחיטה blood does not work either, teaching the stronger case (שחיטה) would have taught the dead-animal case by כל שכן, so the choice of example is strange.

steps.title: The dead-animal case needed to be taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dead-animal case was needed. Otherwise we might think an animal that died is just like one a person killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of a dead animal was needed. You might have thought: What difference is it whether a person killed it or the מלאך המות killed it? So he teaches us that it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי שמעון had to mention the dead animal. Without it, we might have mixed up a dead animal with a killed one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since blood of killed animals does work, one might think an animal that died is also 'killed,' just by the מלאך המות. רבי שמעון teaches that it is not the same. So the ברייתא is still about dead versus killed, and it does not prove that שחיטה blood works.

keyTerms.meaning: He needed to say it, it was necessary
You might have thought to say
The angel of death
So he teaches us otherwise

phrases.english: Blood of the dead animal was necessary for him to teach,
since it could enter your mind to say:
What difference is it to me whether he himself killed it,
or whether the angel of death killed it?
So he teaches us that it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows that the example chosen was needed to teach something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An animal that died is like one killed by a person, so its blood should work too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood of a dead animal is different from blood of a killed animal. The ברייתא is about that contrast, so רב אסי is not disproven.
steps.whatToRemember: The first attack on רב אסי fails: 'dead-animal blood does not work' only contrasts with killed animals, and it had to be said so we would not treat death as a 'killing by the מלאך המות.'

steps.title: Blood of a wound seems to imply slaughter blood works
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says רבי שמעון holds that blood from an animal's wound does not make things susceptible. That seems to imply blood of שחיטה does, which goes against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי שמעון says: Blood of its wound does not make things susceptible. Doesn't that mean that blood of שחיטה does?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second attack on רב אסי, using the same kind of inference as before but from a different ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If blood from a wound does not work, it sounds like blood from שחיטה does work. That again would go against רב אסי's claim that for רבי שמעון the blood does not do it.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood from its wound

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Shimon says:
Blood of its wound does not make things susceptible.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, הָא דַּם שְׁחִיטָה מַכְשִׁיר?
phrases.english: Isn't it that this implies blood of slaughter does make things susceptible?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: דַּם מַגֵּפָתוֹ אֵינוֹ מַכְשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first attack (Steps 11–14) was answered, so the גמרא tries a new ברייתא with the same structure.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that for רבי שמעון the blood does not make the meat susceptible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'blood of a wound does not work' implies blood of שחיטה does work.

steps.title: Again, the opposite case may be killed animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: the contrast may be with blood of killed animals, not blood of שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the implication is that blood of killed animals makes things susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the second attack with the same answer it used in Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood from a wound is set against blood of an animal that was killed, so the ברייתא still tells us nothing about blood of שחיטה.

phrases.english: No, rather blood of killed animals makes things susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the inference in Step 15, the same way Step 12 countered Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference against רב אסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contrast can be with killed animals rather than with שחיטה.

steps.title: But what about slaughter blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to question this answer again: does that mean blood of שחיטה does not make things susceptible?
steps.simpleTranslation: But blood of שחיטה, what? It does not make things susceptible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to the answer in Step 16, just like it did in Step 13. The rest of the challenge and its answer continue right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שחיטה blood does not work, why did רבי שמעון pick the weaker case of a wound? The question has the same shape as Step 13, so expect a similar push and answer next.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דַּם שְׁחִיטָה מַאי, לָא מַכְשִׁיר?
phrases.english: But blood of slaughter, what? It does not make things susceptible?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל דַּם שְׁחִיטָה מַאי, לָא מַכְשִׁיר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to challenge the answer in Step 16, repeating the pattern of Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the wound-blood ברייתא contrasts with killed animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שחיטה blood also does not work, it would have been the better example to teach. The challenge continues past this point.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same question the גמרא asked in Step 13, now about the wound ברייתא. It is not a new topic. The גמרא is running the same test on the second source.

steps.title: Then he should have taught blood of slaughter instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its challenge: if blood of שחיטה does not make food susceptible, רבי שמעון should have taught that, and wound blood would follow with a כל שכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him teach us that blood of slaughter does not make food susceptible, and all the more so the blood of its wound!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it began in the last step. If blood of שחיטה does not make food susceptible, why did רבי שמעון bother to mention wound blood?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of שחיטה is the stronger case, because it is the blood of a proper slaughter. If even that blood does not make food susceptible, then wound blood certainly would not. So stating only the wound case looks like a wasted teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that comes out during kosher slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same kind of question as Step 13. Earlier the contrast was with a dead animal; now it is with wound blood. Do not mix up the two rounds.

phrases.english: Let him teach us blood of slaughter,
phrases.notes: He means: let רבי שמעון say that blood of slaughter does not make food susceptible.

phrases.english: and all the more so the blood of its wound!

steps.triggerLanguage: לַשְׁמְעִינַן דַּם שְׁחִיטָה, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן דַּם מַגֵּפָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading from Step 16, which implies that blood of שחיטה does not make food susceptible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stronger case (blood of שחיטה) does not work, stating the weaker case (wound blood) is unnecessary, since it follows by כל שכן.

steps.title: The wound case was needed on its own
steps.stepSummary: Wound blood had to be taught. Otherwise we might think wounding an animal is like killing it partly, so its blood would work like blood of killed animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary for him to teach the blood of its wound. I might have thought: what difference is it to me if he killed all of it, or killed half of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that wound blood is not a wasted teaching. Without it, we might have treated a wounded animal like a killed one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of killed animals (דם חללים) does make food susceptible. Someone might think a wound is just a partial killing, so wound blood should count the same way. רבי שמעון teaches that it does not, and that is something blood of שחיטה could not have taught us.

keyTerms.meaning: He needed to teach it
You might have thought; a mistaken first assumption
Half

phrases.english: The blood of its wound, he needed to teach it,
since it could enter your mind to say:
What difference is it to me if he killed all of it,
or if he killed half of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּם מַגֵּפָתוֹ אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18, the same way Step 14 answered Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: איצטריך: the case that seemed extra was needed to block a mistaken comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wound is just a partial killing, so wound blood should make food susceptible like blood of killed animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wound blood does not make food susceptible. This is a new point that blood of שחיטה would not have taught.

steps.title: Why does blood of killed animals work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source shows that blood of killed animals makes food susceptible.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about blood of the slain, that it makes food susceptible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of the rule it has been relying on: blood of killed animals makes food susceptible. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole answer so far rests on the idea that דם חללים makes food susceptible. The גמרא wants to know why that blood is different from wound blood or blood of שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is different?
Blood of animals that were killed (not by שחיטה)
Makes food able to become impure

phrases.english: And what is different about blood of the slain, that it makes food susceptible?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule about דם חללים that Steps 16 and 19 assumed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that blood of killed animals makes food susceptible

steps.title: The verse calls it something you drink
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'and drinks blood of the slain.' The blood is described as a drink, so it counts as a liquid that makes food susceptible.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And drinks blood of the slain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that describes the blood of killed animals as something one drinks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only certain liquids make food susceptible. Because the פסוק speaks of drinking דם חללים, the תורה treats this blood as a drinkable liquid, so it makes food susceptible.

keyTerms.meaning: He will drink
A drinkable liquid, the kind that makes food susceptible

phrases.english: As it is written: "And drinks blood of the slain."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק calls דם חללים something one drinks, so it counts as a liquid that makes food susceptible.

steps.title: Blood of slaughter is compared to water too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: there is also a פסוק about blood of שחיטה, comparing it to water. So it should make food susceptible too.
steps.simpleTranslation: About blood of slaughter it is also written: 'Pour it on the ground like water!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that only blood of killed animals has a verse behind it. Blood of שחיטה also has one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water is the most basic liquid that makes food susceptible. If the תורה compares blood of שחיטה to water, that seems to show it also makes food susceptible. That would go against רב אסי and the reading the גמרא has been defending.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
You shall pour it out like water

phrases.english: About blood of slaughter it is also written:
"You shall pour it on the ground like water"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of Step 21 by applying it to blood of שחיטה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that blood of שחיטה does not make food susceptible, while דם חללים does
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a verse that links blood to a liquid makes it susceptible-making, then blood of שחיטה, which is compared to water, should count too.

steps.title: That verse teaches something else
steps.stepSummary: The 'like water' פסוק does not deal with making food susceptible. It teaches that one may benefit from the blood of disqualified קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse comes to permit benefit from the blood of disqualified consecrated animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'like water' פסוק is used for a different law, so it tells us nothing about making food susceptible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as water may be used freely, the blood of פסולי המוקדשין may be used for benefit, even though their meat has restrictions. Since the comparison to water teaches that law, it cannot also show that blood of שחיטה makes food susceptible. So the earlier position stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To permit
Consecrated animals that became disqualified (for example, through a blemish) and were redeemed
Benefit or use

steps.whatToRemember: According to this line: דם חללים makes food susceptible because the פסוק calls it something you drink. Wound blood does not. The 'like water' פסוק about blood of שחיטה teaches that one may benefit from the blood of פסולי המוקדשין, not anything about making food susceptible.

phrases.english: That verse is to permit their blood
of disqualified consecrated animals for benefit
is what it comes for.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לְמִישְׁרֵי דָּמָן דִּפְסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין בַּהֲנָאָה הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is used for a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison of blood of שחיטה to water shows that it makes food susceptible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison to water teaches that one may benefit from the blood of פסולי המוקדשין. It does not show that blood of שחיטה makes food susceptible.
